newsitem.title: TURKEY: Live cement sale hits Turkish screens.
newsitem.headline: Live cement sale hits Turkish screens.

text.p: Turkish television viewers, used to a diet of gore and game shows, have been treated instead to hours of dull live broadcasts of the sale of state-owned factories -- part of official efforts to dispel suspicions of corruption surrounding the privatisation process.
The HBB station beamed around five hours of the auctions for the privatisation of cement, ceramics and refractory plants from a non-descript government office on Thursday.
A commentator explained minute details of the cement business and share offers in an effort to break long silences as businessmen scribbled bids and counter-bids on pieces of paper.

HBB was the only one of 14 national channels to heed a government call to show the proceedings. The broadcast was meant as proof of openness against charges of corruption in Turkey's 10-year-old privatisation process.
Turkey has raised only a fraction of the $2.7 billion it planned to earn from sell-offs this year because of political chaos and constitutional challenges by the opposition.
